title: Segmented canary rollout engine with cohort-aware traffic choreography and probabilistic rollback
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Current rollout policies allow only global, time-based step schedules and are brittle for heterogeneous customer cohorts (mobile vs web, low-latency vs batch). We need a canary configuration/policy engine that supports: segmented traffic splits by cohort attributes, probabilistic (fractional) sampling, shadow probing, A/B branches, and deterministic auto-rollback based on composite SLOs and statistical tests.

Goal: Implement a compact rollout DSL and engine (Segmented Rollout Manifest - SRM) and runtime enforcement that: 1) expresses step schedules keyed by cohort selectors; 2) computes safe traffic allocations with guardrail checks before each step; 3) integrates with telemetry to run Bayesian or sequential hypothesis tests to detect regressions; 4) supports shadow probes and gradual promotion; 5) exposes observability (per-cohort latency/cost/quality) and programmatic rollback triggers.

Constraints: Must be compatible with existing routing layer, not add >5% p50 latency for admission checks, and respect Dedicated/private routing policies. Rollouts must be reversible with an explicit audit log and easy developer UX in the Console.
acceptance_criteria: SRM schema v1 defined and validated against unit tests
Runtime accepts SRM and applies cohort-based traffic splits for staged steps
Guardrail checks (latency, error-rate, model-drift) run automatically before each increase; failures block progress and trigger annotated rollback
Shadow probing mode available: traffic forked to new model with no user-visible exposure and end-to-end traces correlated
Alerting and console UI surfaces per-cohort metrics and recommended rollback reasons
Automatic rollback executes via orchestrator with clear audit trail and safe fallback to previous model variant
End-to-end integration test that simulates a 10kreq/min cohort and verifies rollback within 5 minutes after a 10% latency regression
implementation_notes: 2026-02-12: spike completed — compared sequential probability ratio test vs Bayesian online changepoint detection for rollback decisions; team prefers SPRT for lower compute and deterministic thresholds
2026-02-20: prototype SRM DSL (YAML) sketched; supports cohort selectors, step definitions, guardrail blocks, and rollback policies
Trade-offs: full Bayesian analysis would give richer uncertainty but increases compute and latency; will iterate to a hybrid approach (SPRT for fast blocking, offline Bayesian for post-mortem)

Routing integration: added admission check hook in request path; to keep p50 cost low we evaluate guardrail precondition only on a sampled subset (configurable) and run full check async for final promotion
Privacy: cohort selectors must not leak PII; limiting selectors to request metadata (region, platform, customer_tier) only
Q: how to reconcile Dedicated tenant routing? Answer: SRM produces per-tenant rollout manifests; operator controls whether manifests are honored in Dedicated mode (initially opt-in)
